# Depot turnaround time before and after the revised intake rota: a two-site service evaluation

## Abstract

A revised intake rota was introduced at two depots in March 2021. This
evaluation compares turnaround time in the six months either side of that
change. Median turnaround fell at both sites, and the proportion of units
meeting the four-hour standard rose at both. The weekend comparison is
available for one site only.

## Methods

Turnaround time was measured from the moment a unit was booked in at the
gate to the moment it was released to the yard. Every unit booked in during
the two six-month windows was included; nothing was excluded on the grounds
of duty class or age.

The four-hour standard is the depot's own service target. It was in force
throughout both windows and its definition did not change, so the before and
after proportions are measured against the same line.

Weekday and weekend intakes are reported separately because they are staffed
differently. Site B did not operate a weekend intake before the change, so
its weekend rows carry no before figure rather than a zero.

## Results

Turnaround improved on every measure that both sites report.

[TABLE 1. Median turnaround time by site and rota period, with the proportion of units meeting the four-hour standard.]

The weekday improvement is the larger of the two at Site A and the smaller at
Site B, which is what the difference in their starting positions would
predict. Neither site reached the four-hour standard on every unit in either
period.

## Discussion

The rota change is associated with a fall in turnaround time at both sites,
and the association survives separating weekday from weekend intake at the
one site that reports both. This is a service evaluation and not a trial: no
unit was allocated, and the two windows differ in season as well as in rota.
